items.title: ❗️During the day of September 25, from 07:00 to 18:30, the enemy attacked Ukraine with 162 strike UAVs of various types, including 76 jet-powered ones, as well as Gerbera, Banderol/Dan-T drones and others. According to preliminary data from the Air Force Command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, air defense forces shot down or suppressed 127 UAVs, of which 44 were jet-powered. Hits by enemy air attack assets were also recorded at 27 locations, along with falling debris from downed drones at another 4 locations.

items.title: ❗️The 🇷🇺Perm oil refinery Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez completely halted oil processing after a Ukrainian UAV attack on September 25. According to Reuters sources, inter-shop pipelines, petroleum product storage tanks in the feedstock and product park, and some secondary units were damaged; a fire broke out at the plant and was still burning in the evening. The repair timeline is currently unknown.

items.title: ❗️EU member states have agreed to allocate €6.6 billion from the European Peace Facility for Ukraine. Of this amount, €900 million will go to the EU Military Assistance Mission, €1 billion will fund new joint equipment purchases, and €4.7 billion will reimburse member states for their expenses; some of them have already said they will direct their share straight to Ukraine. This was announced by Kaja Kallas.

items.title: ❗️The Alternative for Germany faction submitted a motion to the Bundestag calling for a rejection of Ukraine’s EU membership, any military security guarantees, and associate status. The party proposes ending all German military and financial aid to Kyiv until “serious” peace talks with Russia begin, while keeping humanitarian assistance. AfD also opposes German funding for Ukraine’s reconstruction and demands privileged German access to Ukrainian rare earth metals and other resources as compensation for loans already provided. The initiative drew a sharp response from other factions: CDU deputy Knut Abraham called it support for Putin, Green MP Robin Wagener described it as a “text written in the Kremlin,” and SPD representative Ralf Stegner said AfD stands on Russia’s side. The motion was referred to committee.

items.title: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung expressed regret that Ukraine disclosed the transfer of North Korean POWs, saying the sides had agreed to keep it confidential. Lee called the repatriation issue highly sensitive because of its implications for diplomacy, national security and the Korean Peninsula. He said he did not know what circumstances led Ukraine to break the agreement, while stressing that Seoul had deliberately pursued the process without publicity. #Ukraine

items.title: Russian state agency RIA Novosti published a commentary titled “Russia faces another special military operation. It will be very short,” focused on Lithuania. The author portrays potential Western nuclear deployments in Lithuania as a threat that could force Moscow to act, argues a military conflict in the Baltics would be brief due to geography, and explicitly raises the possibility of Russia using nuclear-armed missiles without deploying ground forces, calling such an outcome “lightning-fast.” #Lithuania
